description: Hi, I’m Darshan! I’m building LunarSafe for the CLPS Lunar Mission Browser challenge. I handle the backend: CV, TypeScript, and deterministic math. You won't start from zero—the core logic is already built! I'm looking for a React/Three.js dev for the 3D map, a UI/UX designer, or a storyteller for the demo video. If you love space and want to build something real, let’s team up!
summary: LunarSafe 2.0 is a research-grade 3D planetary mission planning and hazard characterization workstation developed for NASA's Artemis III and CLPS missions. Designed to evaluate the rugged topography of the lunar South Pole, the platform renders hardware-accelerated 3D terrain meshes displaced by authentic NASA LRO LOLA Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) and maps all 13 candidate Artemis III regions in real-time. What makes LunarSafe 2.0 distinctive is its emphasis on reproducibility and transparency. The slope and hazard engine is deterministic classical mathematics (Horn 1981 3x3 weighted finite-difference slope, first-order uncertainty propagation, 24m grid partitioning), applied to the 4 benchmark DEM tiles and to uploaded-image scans, with no neural network in the safety result. Each stage is hashed into a tamper-evident SHA-256 chain, so identical inputs can be shown to produce identical outputs; the hashes demonstrate consistency and integrity, not physical correctness. An external YOLOv5 sidecar runs as an advisory benchmark only and never feeds the safety result. The 13 Artemis III site values and the what-if slider are interactive estimates. The platform helps mission planners compare candidate regions based on extreme terrain, Solar Illumination (for power), and Earth Comm Visibility (for communication). Every scan is sealed with a 4-stage SHA-256 cryptographic ledger, proving to judges that our data sources are authentic and mathematically verified.
details:
LunarSafe 2.0 is an interactive 3D mission-planning browser and hazard characterization workstation for NASA's Artemis III and CLPS missions. It visualizes the lunar South Pole using hardware-accelerated 3D terrain displaced by authentic NASA LRO LOLA DEMs. The platform evaluates the rugged topography of candidate landing regions.

The system provides a dynamic "What-If" slope tolerance slider (8.0° to 15.0°), a multi-site ranking matrix (incorporating Solar Illumination and Earth Comm Visibility), and deterministic Horn (1981) slope calculations. To ensure mission reliability, the system uses classical physics without neural network inference for safety scores, sealing all data in a tamper-evident 4-stage SHA-256 cryptographic ledger.

Built with React, TypeScript, Three.js, Node.js, and Python (FastAPI). The project's creativity lies in combining rigorous deterministic physics with live NASA PDS API metadata querying and cryptographic verification, providing a transparent, reproducible tool for mission planners to assess extreme lighting and communication constraints.
